clue.text: Abstract esoteric polish paper dealing with the economy

indicators.note: esoteric means obscure or strange, so the letters of polish are made strange by rearranging them

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, the British newspaper of business and economics

explanation.surface: An obscure abstract on polishing printed in a financial newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'esoteric' rearranges POLISH into SHOPLI. 'Abstract' is a verb here: to abstract is to take away, to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstract can mean to remove or steal, and shoplifting is stealing goods from a store.

clue.text: Carol carries a royal garment

indicators.note: one word carries another inside it, so the song holds the other letters within it

parts.note: a carol is a song, especially a Christmas one
R is a standard abbreviation for royal, as in RN for Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Someone called Carol is carrying a piece of clothing fit for royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name, but it is the Christmas song. 'carries' puts A and R inside SONG.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarong is a length of cloth wrapped round the waist, worn in South-East Asia: a type of clothing.

clue.text: Start introduction to thermodynamics during open university class

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits within it, so this letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: OU is the Open University, the UK's distance-learning university
a set is a class or group, as in a school maths set

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A student begins a thermodynamics module in an Open University class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class' suggests a lecture group, but here it is a set; 'during' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The outset is the very beginning of something, its starting point.

clue.text: A dangerously attractive lady learning exotic flower arrangement

parts.note: lore is knowledge or learning handed down
a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers, an arrangement from a distant land

explanation.surface: A seductive woman is learning the art of exotic flower arranging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' is not an anagram signal: it marks the lei as foreign, from Hawaii.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is the siren of German legend whose song lured Rhine boatmen to their deaths, so a byword for a fatal temptress.

clue.text: Two thirds of a large bottle makes you droop

indicators.note: keeping two thirds of a six-letter word means dropping its last third, two letters

parts.note: a flagon is a large bottle or jug for wine or cider

explanation.surface: Drinking two thirds of a big bottle leaves you wilting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two thirds of' keeps four of FLAGON's six letters, dropping the final ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to lose energy and sag, to become tired or weak.

clue.text: To communicate one politician requires skill

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MP is Member of Parliament
art is skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: For one politician to get a message across takes real skill.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart is to pass on or tell information, to make it known.

clue.text: Experts in vermin control sort out our mess

indicators.note: sorting out a mess means putting its parts into a new arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pest controllers are asked to come and deal with our messy home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort out' rearranges OUR MESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousers are cats good at catching mice, so skilled at keeping vermin down.

clue.text: Cloudy substance containing corrosive chemicals

parts.note: reads like a lab description of a murky liquid; cryptically it is precipitation falling from clouds, polluted with acids

explanation.definitionFit: This rain carries dissolved sulphur and nitrogen oxides that damage stonework and forests: falling from clouds and corrosive.

clue.text: What female hunter wants in concert

definitions.meaning: someone hunting a woman wants to win her over, a phrase heard as three words

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads the answer as a three-word phrase: a man chasing a woman wants 'to get her'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunting a woman is aiming to win her; doing things in concert means doing them jointly, side by side.

clue.text: Go off song by new club member

parts.note: to go off is to rot, as food does
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: A performer launches into a song for the benefit of a newly joined member.
explanation.walkthrough: The club is Rotary International, a service organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rotarian belongs to a Rotary Club, part of the international service organisation.

clue.text: Making better item of jewellery with copper on the front

indicators.note: the copper piece is placed at the front of the other, ahead of it in the answer

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a ring is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: Improving a ring by plating its front with copper.
explanation.definitionFit: Curing a patient is healing them, restoring them to health.

clue.text: Bacon, perhaps, and a drink outside the queen

indicators.note: the drink is placed outside, wrapping round the single letter

parts.note: a pint is a drink of beer
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: Bacon and a drink are served outside to the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bacon' looks like breakfast food but is Francis Bacon, the British painter. 'outside' puts PINT round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was a celebrated 20th-century British artist working in oils.

clue.text: Want large key in order to wind up

parts.note: to want something is to need it
L is the size abbreviation for large
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: You need a large key in order to wind up a clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind up' is British slang for tease or provoke, not winding a clockwork mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to annoy or provoke them, just as winding them up does.

clue.text: Extremely terrible conflict about strikebreaker is a beastly thing

indicators.note: the conflict goes about the letters, holding them inside

parts.note: war is armed conflict

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the first and last letters of terrible

parts.note: a rat is a worker who breaks a strike, a scab

explanation.surface: A terrible war over a strikebreaker is a brutal business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly' suggests nastiness, but the definition is literal: an actual beast. 'Extremely' and 'about' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small animal living by rivers, so a beast in the literal sense.

clue.text: Barge touring strait with rare bird

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the barge goes round the letters

parts.note: a keel is a flat-bottomed barge used on rivers such as the Tyne
St is an abbreviation for strait in place names
R is an abbreviation for rare, used in grading coins

explanation.surface: Birdwatchers on a barge cruising through a strait spot an unusual bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rare bird' looks like the definition, but a kestrel is common; 'rare' supplies a letter and 'touring' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A kestrel is a small falcon known for hovering over roadside verges.

clue.text: Is broken sedan found in river? Up you get then!

indicators.note: something found in a place sits inside it, so these letters go inside the river

parts.note: the Rhine is a major European river

indicators.note: a broken thing has its parts out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wrecked car has been found in a river; time to get up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sedan' sounds like the car, but it is only letters to be jumbled by 'broken'; 'found in' puts the run inside the river after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase is the cheery call to wake someone and get them out of bed.

clue.text: Latin's funny with mad historian

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters come out in an odd order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A mad historian finds Latin hilarious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' rearranges LATIN and MAD. F. W. Maitland was a great English legal historian.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederic William Maitland (1850-1906) wrote the classic history of English law.

clue.text: Big fall makes you depressed and reportedly broke

parts.note: to feel down is to be depressed

indicators.note: reportedly means as said by others, so a word heard rather than seen

parts.note: broke means poor, having no money

explanation.surface: A big fall in the market leaves you depressed and broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' gives the word for broke said out loud, which matches a word for flowing heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: A downpour is a heavy fall of rain.

clue.text: Tracheotomy — one new thing science students learn about

indicators.note: a new version of the letters is a fresh arrangement of them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Medical students treat a tracheotomy as a new topic to study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges TRACHEOTOMY plus I from 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idea that matter is made of tiny particles is a basic theory taught in physics and chemistry.

clue.text: 10 _____ cooked up could be nauseating

indicators.note: cooked up means mixed together, so these letters plus the others are rearranged into the last word

parts.note: the letters of this word are the pool that the rearrangement makes
ten is the number written as a figure

explanation.surface: Ten lizards cooked into a dish might make you sick.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the blank: TEN and the answer, 'cooked up', make NAUSEATING. The 10 looks like a cross-reference to 10 across but is just the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Iguanas are large tropical lizards, eaten in Central America, which many would find a stomach-turning dish.

clue.text: Playing a louder part of a song

indicators.note: playing with letters means moving them about, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician plays one section of a song more loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' rearranges A LOUDER.
explanation.definitionFit: In singing, a roulade is a rapid run of ornamental notes sung on one syllable.

clue.text: Soldier restraining artist who has offended stars

indicators.note: restraining means holding back, so the soldier holds the artist inside

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
Tracey Emin is the British artist whose provocative work, such as her unmade bed, has caused offence

explanation.surface: A soldier holds back an artist who has upset some celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' suggests celebrities, but means a constellation; 'restraining' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the Twins, is a constellation and sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: United spread dirt about premier's first sporting official

parts.note: U is an abbreviation for United, as in football club names

indicators.note: the mud goes about the letter, surrounding it

parts.note: to mire is to spatter or cover with mud

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Manchester United fans sling mud at the Prime Minister's top referee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts P, from 'premier's first', inside MIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: An umpire is the official who rules on play in sports such as cricket and tennis.

clue.text: How head of the priory appeared after severe cuts were made?

definitions.text: How head of the priory appeared after severe cuts were made?

parts.words: How head of the priory appeared after severe cuts were made?
parts.note: reads like budget cuts at a priory; really it is the prior's head after a monastic haircut shaved the crown

explanation.definitionFit: A monk's head is shaved on top as a sign of religious devotion, leaving a ring of hair.

clue.text: Employ parent around gallery

indicators.note: the parent goes around the other word, which sits inside

parts.note: mum is a mother, a parent
to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: Get your mother to take you round an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gallery' is the definition, not part of the wordplay; 'around' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallery is a building displaying art or exhibits, as a museum does.

clue.text: Brewer's top beer is something bound to transport

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: The brewery's best beer is sure to delight drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to transport' looks like 'sure to delight', but means tied up for carrying.
explanation.definitionFit: A bale is a large bundle of hay or goods tied with twine for moving.

clue.text: Supply a horse to ride

parts.note: a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to provide a horse for riding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: a quantity of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A supply of something is a quantity of it, how much is available.

clue.text: Brilliant old fiddler hiding silver in Italian bread

indicators.note: hiding means keeping something inside out of view, so the bread holds the silver

parts.note: panini are Italian bread rolls, often toasted
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A crooked old violinist conceals stolen silver inside an Italian sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddler' looks like a cheat, but means a violinist; 'hiding' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Niccolò Paganini (1782-1840) was a virtuoso violinist and composer.

clue.text: Pressure unionist to wear formal clothes outside

indicators.note: the formal clothes go outside, around the letter

parts.note: dress, as in evening dress, is formal clothing
U is an abbreviation for Unionist, as in Northern Irish party names

explanation.surface: A trade unionist is pressured to wear a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts DRESS round U, as a wearer is inside clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is pressure or threats used to force someone to act against their will.

clue.text: Cardinal free to roam about island — volcanic one

parts.note: ten is a cardinal number

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the island letter, surrounding it
to roam is to wander freely, so the letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: A cardinal is free to wander around a volcanic island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' looks like a churchman but is a cardinal number. 'to roam' rearranges FREE as ERFE and 'about' puts it round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenerife in the Canary Islands is dominated by the volcano Mount Teide.
